topStories.headline: Hawks Face Harker Heights Tonight in First 6A Bi-District Playoff Game
topStories.dek: The Red Oak Hawks (6-4) make their 6A playoff debut this evening against Killeen Harker Heights at Leo Buckley Stadium.
topStories.body:
Red Oak High School's football team tips off its first-ever Class 6A Division II bi-district playoff appearance tonight, Friday, November 13, when the Hawks (6-4) travel to Killeen to face Harker Heights (7-3) at Leo Buckley Stadium, with kickoff set for 7 p.m.

The matchup caps a historic regular season for a Red Oak program navigating its first year at the 6A level. The Hawks finished the regular season fourth in their district after dropping their final tune-up game, 62-3, at North Crowley on November 5. Despite the lopsided loss, the team qualified for the postseason bracket released by UIL on November 8.

Scouting reports published ahead of the game flag Harker Heights' run game as a potential factor, with the Knights entering as the higher seed. The winner advances to the area round, scheduled for November 19-21, and would face a playoff survivor from the Longview-Rowlett bracket.

Tickets are available through GoFan. Fans who cannot travel to Killeen are encouraged to follow live updates through MaxPreps and the Red Oak ISD athletics page.

topStories.headline: FBI Raids Midlothian Oil and Gas Firm Facing Fraud Allegations
topStories.dek: Federal agents descended on three homes and a business in Midlothian on November 6 as part of a multi-agency investigation into West Texas Crude Energy, LLC.
topStories.body:
On the morning of November 6, FBI agents and other law enforcement officials executed simultaneous search warrants at three residences and a business in Midlothian, all connected to an oil and gas development company called West Texas Crude Energy, LLC, located on 9th Street. The FBI confirmed its involvement in the raids, which were part of a broader investigation. Midlothian police issued a statement saying there was no active threat to the public.

The company has faced multiple civil fraud lawsuits. Texas Railroad Commission records cited in one of those suits reportedly show no active production for any well on which West Texas Crude Energy is listed as the operator — a detail that has fueled allegations that investors may have been misled about the firm's actual operations.

As of this writing, no criminal charges have been publicly filed, and the investigation is ongoing. The FBI has not disclosed the full scope of what agents were seeking. My Town News will continue to follow the case as federal investigators and prosecutors make further information available.

topStories.headline: Red Oak Data Center Lawsuit Remains Active as State Permit Freeze Continues
topStories.dek: A lawsuit challenging the city's approval of an 830-acre Compass Datacenters rezoning is still pending in Ellis County court, with no ruling reported as of early November.
topStories.body:
Two Red Oak property owners — Elda Jazmin Villegas and Kathleen Estelle Heifrin — filed suit on September 1 in the 40th Judicial District Court in Ellis County, naming the City of Red Oak, Mayor Mark L. Stanfill, and five council members as defendants. The plaintiffs, who own property within 200 feet of the disputed land, allege that the ordinance rezoning roughly 830 acres of agricultural land for Compass DataCenters' planned campus was not lawfully adopted. The case was still pending with no ruling reported as of early November 2026.

The rezoning itself cleared the Red Oak City Council by a 4-1 vote in May 2026, over strong opposition from residents who packed City Hall for a meeting that stretched past midnight. Critics cited noise, traffic, water demand, and the effect on the community's residential character. City officials argued the project — one of seven data center sites now operating or planned within Red Oak's 16 square miles — could generate a projected $13 billion in investment and significantly expand the tax base without raising residential taxes.

At the state level, Governor Greg Abbott in September directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to stop issuing permits sought by data centers pending an ERCOT audit of every facility in its interconnection queue. That freeze adds an additional layer of uncertainty for the Compass campus, though the governor's order does not directly resolve the local legal dispute. Residents' groups have separately petitioned for a statewide moratorium on new construction. The Ellis County court case remains the most direct avenue for neighbors seeking to block the project.

moreNews.headline: MISD's Ninth Elementary School Design Moving Forward in Goodland
moreNews.body: Midlothian ISD's Bond 2025 program continued to advance this month, with the Midlothian Mirror reporting on November 4 that behind-the-scenes design work on Elementary School No. 9 — to be built in the Goodland area of the district — is progressing. Trustees received a project update at the October 19 school board meeting. The school was the cornerstone of Proposition A in the November 2025 bond election, which voters approved. An oversight committee formed in April 2026 is tracking all Bond 2025 projects, including the new elementary, a future Career and Technical Education center, and renovations at Midlothian High School and Frank Seale Middle School.

moreNews.headline: Red Oak ISD Named a CTE District of Distinction by State Association
moreNews.body: Red Oak ISD announced it has been selected as a Career and Technical Education (CTE) District of Distinction by the Career and Technical Association of Texas (CTAT). The recognition, posted on the district's website, celebrates districts that demonstrate exemplary leadership and innovation in CTE programs. No date for the official award presentation was listed on the district's news page.

moreNews.headline: TxDOT Lane and Ramp Closures on I-35E at Ovilla Road Through Mid-November
moreNews.body: The Texas Department of Transportation has scheduled overnight and daytime construction closures along southbound I-35E near Ovilla and Red Oak through at least November 15. Affected areas include the southbound Ovilla Road off-ramp (closed nightly 9 p.m.–9 a.m., November 13–15), southbound I-35E main lanes from the Ovilla off-ramp to Plaza Drive (9 p.m.–5 a.m.), and southbound lanes between Norton Road and Plaza Drive during daytime hours through November 9–December 14. Traffic is being diverted to frontage roads. Drivers are advised to allow extra travel time or use alternate routes.
